# MCP tools, resources and prompts

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/gen_docs.py - do not edit by hand. Regenerate with: uv run python scripts/gen_docs.py -->

The `hpclab mcp serve` server (stdio) exposes the tools, resources and prompts below. It is a thin
frontend: every call is forwarded to the local controller, which validates it with the same
schemas, runs the service and returns an envelope. Input schemas are derived from the service
signatures; parameter prose comes from `src/hpclab/mcp/catalog.py`.

* `structuredContent` of a tool result is the complete envelope; the text block is a short rendering
  (summary, the ids needed for the next call, warnings, `Next:` suggestions).
* Mutations take an `idempotency_key`: retrying with the same key and arguments returns the stored
  result; the same key with other arguments is `idempotency_conflict`. Mutations of versioned state
  (attempts, workflows) also take `expected_version`.
* Annotations (read-only, destructive, ...) are UI hints for the client, never authorization: the
  runtime still checks idempotency, the execution claim, live job identity and the budget.
* Lists default to 20 items (max 100); text reads default to 32 KiB (max 64 KiB).

Contents: [server instructions](#server-instructions) · [result envelope](#result-envelope) ·
[error codes](#error-codes) · [tools (17)](#tools) · [resources](#resources) ·
[prompts (5)](#prompts) · [controller methods](#controller-methods)

## Server instructions

Sent to the client at initialization (`instructions`):

```text
HPC Lab runs ML experiments on Slurm clusters reliably and keeps a ledger linking every reported number to code, config, Slurm job and output digests. Typical flow: cluster_inspect → experiment_prepare (read every validation finding) → workflow_submit (whole matrix; smoke gate first) or run_submit (one run) — confirm GPU spend with the user → runs_list(view='grid') / run_inspect to watch → run_recover + run_submit for failures → evaluation_collect → results_compare → evidence_export → evidence_verify(tex_paths) before submission.
Rules: never resubmit a run whose submission is 'submission_uncertain' (U) — the controller reconciles it; never cancel by guessing a job id — use run_cancel; 'unchecked' / 'unavailable' / 'stale' are not success; report missing or failed seeds, never drop them; numbers for papers come from evidence bundles, not from logs. Mutations take an idempotency_key: reuse it when retrying the same request. Jobs take minutes to days: after a submit, check back after poll_after_ms (or when the user asks) instead of polling in a tight loop. Each result's text ends with 'Next:' suggestions (exact calls with the ids to use); the full data is in structuredContent. Resources: hpclab://experiments (all experiments, newest first — start here in a new session), experiments/<id>, operations/<id>, plans/<id> (+/script), workflows/<id> (current version), runs/<id>, artifacts/<id>, evaluations/<id>, comparisons/<id>, evidence/<id> (+/table.tex, /summary.md, /table.csv, /manifest.json), trace/<bundle_id>:<cell_id>.
```

## Result envelope

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `schema_version` | string | Envelope schema version. |
| `request_id` | string | Id of this request (also in the controller log). |
| `ok` | boolean | `false` when `error` is set. |
| `data` | any | The tool's result (see each tool); may hold confirmed partial data when `ok` is false. |
| `error` | `ErrorInfo` \| null | `{code, message, retryable, operation_ref?, details}` (codes below). |
| `coverage` | `Coverage` \| null | Which sources were consulted and how fresh they were; `complete: false` means something could not be checked. |
| `observed_at` | string \| null | When the underlying observation was made (UTC, ISO 8601). |
| `next_cursor` | string \| null | Continue a paginated read with this cursor. |
| `warnings` | array of string | Things the caller should read before acting. |
| `summary` | string | One line an agent reads first: state and next step. |

`coverage.sources[]` entries are `{name, status, observed_at, detail}` with status `ok`, `cached`, `stale`, `partial`, `unavailable`, `unsupported`, `unauthorized`, `skipped`. Anything but `ok`, `cached` or `skipped` makes `coverage.complete` false: an empty list with
incomplete coverage is *not* "nothing exists".

## Error codes

| code | retryable | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `invalid_argument` |  | The request is malformed (schema, ids of the wrong kind, bad values); `details.errors` lists them. |
| `not_found` |  | No such experiment, plan, run, attempt, artifact, ... in this ledger. |
| `unauthorized` |  | An identity or ownership check failed (e.g. a path escaping the attempt directory). |
| `auth_required` | yes | SSH needs interactive authentication (MFA/Duo, expired ControlMaster). The user runs `hpclab auth <cluster>` in their own terminal; blocked work resumes afterwards. |
| `unsupported` |  | The cluster or profile lacks a capability (e.g. accounting disabled, `runtime.container`). |
| `stale` |  | The referenced content changed since it was indexed or observed; nothing newer is returned silently. |
| `truncated` |  | Reserved. In v0.1 no call fails with it: a result cut at a size bound comes back `ok` with `truncated: true` in `data` and a `next_cursor` / `next_offset` to continue. |
| `ambiguous` |  | More than one plausible match (e.g. a reused Slurm job id); hpclab refuses to guess. |
| `unavailable` | yes | A remote source is down or timed out, or a deadline passed. Retry later. |
| `idempotency_conflict` |  | The idempotency key was already used with different arguments. |
| `version_conflict` |  | `expected_version` is not the current version; `details.current_version` has it. |
| `not_ready` | yes | The target is not ready yet (plan still preparing, probe pending, ...). Retry later. |
| `precondition_failed` |  | The request is valid but the state does not allow it (e.g. request_checkpoint without a declared checkpoint signal). |
| `admission_denied` |  | The single admission gate refused: execution claim held, plan consumed, smoke gate, concurrency slots, dispatch closed. |
| `budget_exceeded` |  | The experiment's GPU-hour budget cannot cover the reservation (GPUs x time limit). |
| `submission_uncertain` |  | On an operation: the submission's outcome is unknown and is being reconciled, or waits for a human (`hpclab resolve`); e.g. a cancel queued behind it. Never resubmit. |
| `policy_violation` |  | The site profile's policy forbids the request. |
| `limit_exceeded` |  | A hard bound was exceeded (matrix > 256 cells, snapshot too large, page too big). |
| `controller_unavailable` | yes | The local controller could not be reached or started. |
| `internal` |  | An unexpected error; details are in the controller log under the request id. |

### cluster_inspect

**Inspect a Slurm cluster** — read-only · idempotent · open-world · controller method `cluster_inspect` (`hpclab.services.cluster:cluster_inspect`)

Check a registered cluster before using it. One entry per check with status ok|warn|fail|unavailable|unsupported|skipped, findings and remediation: auth (SSH/MFA state and the exact command the user must run), identity, scheduler (Slurm version, accounting, PrivateData), storage/quota, runtime tools on the login node, my queue (hpclab-managed vs other jobs), GPU capacity per partition and type, limits, drained or locally suspect nodes, profile facts. Read-only; only bounded metadata commands run on the login node. Unknown data is reported as unavailable, never as zero. candidate_shapes adds low-confidence `sbatch --test-only` start estimates for up to 3 placements.

**Parameters**

| name | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cluster_id` | string | yes |  | Registered cluster id, e.g. 'sim' or 'hai' (the user registers clusters with `hpclab cluster add`). |
| `checks` | array of `"auth"` \| `"identity"` \| `"scheduler"` \| `"storage"` \| `"runtime"` \| `"queue"` \| `"capacity"` \| `"limits"` \| `"nodes"` \| `"profile_facts"` |  |  | Subset of checks to run. Default: all of auth, identity, scheduler, storage, runtime, queue, capacity, limits, nodes, profile_facts. |
| `candidate_shapes` | array of `CandidateShape` |  |  | Up to 3 placements to compare expected start times for, e.g. [{"partition": "gpu", "gpu_type": "a100", "gpus": 1, "time": "04:00:00"}]. |

`CandidateShape`: A placement to compare: ``gpus`` is the job total (spread over ``nodes``).

| field | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `partition` | string | yes |  | Partition name. |
| `gpu_type` | string |  |  | GPU type, e.g. 'a100' (default: any). |
| `gpus` | integer (0..64) |  | `1` | Total GPUs of the job (spread over nodes). |
| `time` | string |  | `"01:00:00"` | Time limit, Slurm format, e.g. '04:00:00' or '1-00:00:00'. |
| `nodes` | integer (1..64) |  | `1` | Number of nodes (default 1). |

**Result `data` fields**

`cluster_id`: string, `status`: `"ok"` | `"warn"` | `"fail"`, `checks`: array of `CheckResult`, `candidates`?: array of `CandidateEstimate`, `remediation`?: array of string.

(`?` = optional. Nested types are in the tool's `outputSchema`.)

### experiment_prepare

**Freeze an experiment plan** — mutating · idempotent · open-world · controller method `experiment_prepare` (`hpclab.services.experiments:experiment_prepare`)

Freeze an ExperimentSpec into an immutable plan: snapshots the project code (content-addressed, git-aware, secrets excluded), creates one Run per matrix cell (plus the smoke run) with its execution plan, and validates everything. Nothing is submitted. Returns experiment_id, plan_id, status ready|preparing|invalid, plan_hash (only when ready), runs[] (run_id, label, exec_plan_hash), GPU-hours vs budget, resource advice from past runs and validation findings: severity 'block' must be fixed (e.g. torch CUDA build newer than the driver, editable install bypassing the snapshot, time above the partition max); 'unchecked' means it could not be verified. status 'preparing' (large project) returns operation_ref to poll. Give spec_path (YAML) or spec. Each new idempotency_key prepares a NEW experiment; to add seeds or cells to an existing one use extends + add_seeds/add_matrix (finished cells are reused, not duplicated); to change one run use derive_from. Next step: workflow_submit(plan_id, plan_hash) for the whole matrix.

**Parameters**

| name | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `idempotency_key` | string | yes |  | Your key for this request. Retrying with the same key and arguments (e.g. after a lost reply) returns the original result; reusing it with other arguments is rejected. Use a new key for a new request. |
| `spec` | object |  |  | ExperimentSpec as an object (alternative to spec_path): name, cluster, entrypoint.argv, matrix, seeds, resources, outputs, smoke, budget, evaluation, comparison. code.project_root defaults to the working directory. |
| `spec_path` | string |  |  | Path to an ExperimentSpec YAML, e.g. 'hpclab.yaml'. Relative paths resolve against the agent's working directory; the spec's code.project_root resolves against the YAML's directory. |
| `cluster_id` | string |  |  | Override spec.cluster (a registered cluster id). |
| `experiment` | string |  |  | Override spec.name (the experiment name). |
| `matrix` | object of array of string \| integer \| number \| boolean \| null |  |  | Override spec.matrix, e.g. {"method": ["baseline", "mixup"]}. Seeds stay in spec.seeds. |
| `extends` | string |  |  | experiment_id to extend with new cells (use with add_seeds and/or add_matrix). Only the new cells get runs. |
| `add_seeds` | array of integer |  |  | Seeds to add to every cell when extending, e.g. [4, 5]. |
| `add_matrix` | object of array of string \| integer \| number \| boolean \| null |  |  | Extra values per matrix axis when extending, e.g. {"method": ["cutmix"]}. |
| `derive_from` | `DeriveFrom` |  |  | Derive a new run from an existing one with changed params/resources/argv, e.g. {"run_id": "run_...", "overrides": {"params": {"lr": 0.05}}}. The original run is untouched. |
| `overrides` | array of `ValidationOverride` |  |  | [{check, reason}] to downgrade a blocking finding to a warning. Only with the user's explicit agreement; recorded in the ledger. |
| `validate_remote` | boolean |  | `true` | Run the bounded remote checks (venv, torch CUDA build vs driver, sbatch --test-only). Default true; false skips them (those findings become 'unchecked'). |

`DeriveFrom`

| field | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `run_id` | string | yes |  | Run to derive from. |
| `overrides` | `DeriveOverrides` |  |  | What changes: {params?, resources?, argv_append?}. |
| `recapture_code` | boolean |  | `false` | Snapshot the project code again instead of reusing the original run's snapshot. |

`DeriveOverrides`: What changes in a derived Run (a changed RunSpec is always a *new* Run).

| field | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `params` | object of string \| integer \| number \| boolean \| null |  |  | Parameter changes, e.g. {"lr": 0.05} (placeholders in argv are re-rendered). |
| `resources` | object |  |  | Resource changes, e.g. {"mem": "32G", "time": "08:00:00"}. |
| `argv_append` | array of string |  |  | Extra arguments appended to the entrypoint argv. |

`ValidationOverride`: Explicit, audited decision to proceed despite a blocking finding.

| field | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `check` | string | yes |  | Name of the blocking check to downgrade (validation.findings[].check). |
| `reason` | string | yes |  | The user's reason (recorded). |

### run_submit

**Submit one run** — mutating · idempotent · open-world · controller method `run_submit` (`hpclab.services.submission:run_submit`)

Submit ONE prepared run to Slurm (for a whole matrix use workflow_submit). Returns a receipt at once (attempt_id, operation_ref, poll_after_ms) — the receipt is NOT proof that Slurm accepted the job; check run_inspect(run_id) or the operation after poll_after_ms. A run has at most one active execution: a second submit (even with another key) is refused while an attempt is active or its submission is uncertain. The smoke gate and budget are enforced. Spends GPU-hours: confirm with the user first.

**Parameters**

| name | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `run_id` | string | yes |  | Run to execute (runs[].run_id from experiment_prepare, or run_id from run_recover). |
| `execution_plan_hash` | string | yes |  | The exec_plan_hash to execute: runs[].exec_plan_hash from experiment_prepare, or exec_plan_hash from run_recover. Each execution plan can be used once. |
| `idempotency_key` | string | yes |  | Your key for this request. Retrying with the same key and arguments (e.g. after a lost reply) returns the original result; reusing it with other arguments is rejected. Use a new key for a new request. |
| `force_without_gate` | boolean |  | `false` | Submit a main run before its smoke gate passed. Requires reason; avoid unless the user insists. |
| `reason` | string |  |  | Why the smoke gate is bypassed (recorded in the ledger). Required with force_without_gate. |

**Result `data` fields**

`operation_ref`: string, `operation_id`: string, `attempt_id`: string, `run_id`: string, `phase`: string, `poll_after_ms`: integer, `reserved_gpu_hours`: number.

(`?` = optional. Nested types are in the tool's `outputSchema`.)

### workflow_submit

**Dispatch an experiment matrix** — mutating · idempotent · open-world · controller method `workflow_submit` (`hpclab.services.workflows:workflow_submit`)

Dispatch every run of a prepared plan, at most max_parallel active at once; the controller keeps dispatching after the chat ends and survives restarts. The smoke run goes first; main cells start only after it COMPLETED with valid outputs (gate). A circuit breaker pauses dispatch after 2 cells fail with the same environment error. One workflow per plan: calling it again for the same plan returns admission_denied with the existing workflow_id. Returns workflow_id, state, gate and cells; watch progress with runs_list(experiment_id, view='grid'). To resume a paused (circuit breaker) or gate_failed workflow after the fix, pass workflow_id + resume_dispatch=true + expected_version (the current version from hpclab://workflows/<workflow_id>). Spends GPU-hours: confirm with the user first.

**Parameters**

| name | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `idempotency_key` | string | yes |  | Your key for this request. Retrying with the same key and arguments (e.g. after a lost reply) returns the original result; reusing it with other arguments is rejected. Use a new key for a new request. |
| `plan_id` | string |  |  | Plan to dispatch: plan_id from experiment_prepare, or the recovery plan_id from run_recover(selector=...). |
| `prepared_experiment_id` | string |  |  | Alternative to plan_id: dispatch the experiment's latest ready plan. |
| `plan_hash` | string |  |  | Optional guard: the plan_hash returned by experiment_prepare. Dispatch is refused if the plan differs from the one reviewed. |
| `max_parallel` | integer |  |  | Max simultaneously active cells, 1-256 (default: spec budget.max_parallel, else site policy). |
| `failure_policy` | `FailurePolicy` |  |  | Circuit-breaker settings, e.g. {"circuit_breaker": {"enabled": true, "threshold": 2}}. Default: enabled, threshold 2, environment failures only. |
| `workflow_id` | string |  |  | Existing workflow to resume (only with resume_dispatch=true). |
| `resume_dispatch` | boolean |  | `false` | Re-open dispatch of a paused workflow (breaker tripped) or a gate_failed one (the smoke run passed after a recovery), once the cause was fixed. Needs workflow_id and expected_version; takes no other options. |
| `expected_version` | integer |  |  | The workflow's current version (from hpclab://workflows/<workflow_id>); required with resume_dispatch. A stale version gets version_conflict with details.current_version. |

`FailurePolicy`

| field | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `circuit_breaker` | `CircuitBreakerPolicy` |  |  | Circuit breaker settings. |

`CircuitBreakerPolicy`: Pause dispatch when ``threshold`` distinct cells fail with the same fingerprint of a listed diagnosis category. Infrastructure/resource failures are never counted.

| field | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean |  | `true` | Pause dispatch when cells keep failing the same way (default true). |
| `threshold` | integer (2..64) |  | `2` | Distinct failing cells with the same fingerprint before pausing (default 2). |
| `categories` | array of `"environment"` \| `"program"` \| `"numerics"` \| `"results"` |  |  | Diagnosis categories that count: environment (default), program, numerics, results. |
| `include_rejections` | boolean |  | `true` | Also count identical sbatch refusals (bad account, bad gres, ...). Default true. |

**Result `data` fields**

`workflow_id`: string, `workflow_ref`: string, `experiment_id`: string, `plan_id`: string, `plan_kind`: string, `plan_hash`: string, `operation_id`: string, `operation_ref`: string, `poll_after_ms`?: integer, `state`: string, `dispatch_state`: string, `version`: integer, `max_parallel`: integer, `planned_run_count`: integer, `skipped_count`: integer, `gate`?: `GateInfo` | null, `resumed`?: boolean, `cells`?: array of `WorkflowCell`.

(`?` = optional. Nested types are in the tool's `outputSchema`.)

### runs_list

**List runs / experiment grid** — read-only · idempotent · closed-world · controller method `runs_list` (`hpclab.services.runs:runs_list`)

Runs of an experiment or workflow from the ledger (fast; no cluster calls beyond the controller's shared poll). view='grid' returns a rows × cols matrix of the main runs (default: treatment axes × seed) with one code per cell: V valid result, R running, Q queued, S submitting, P not dispatched, E completed, evaluation pending (not a failure; evaluation_collect if it persists), F failed (with the diagnosis), C! completed but outputs or evaluation invalid, U submission uncertain (do not resubmit), X cancelled/rejected (incl. cells of a cancelled workflow), ? stale observation. metric='acc' puts the validated value in V cells. view='list' (default) returns one row per run incl. the smoke run, with the latest attempt (attempt_id, job_id, phase, pending reason, progress). The result carries changes_cursor: pass it back as changed_since to get only runs that changed since.

**Parameters**

| name | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `experiment_id` | string |  |  | Experiment to list (experiment_id from experiment_prepare; resource hpclab://experiments lists them, newest first). The grid needs this or workflow_id. |
| `workflow_id` | string |  |  | Workflow to list (alternative to experiment_id). |
| `states` | array of `RunStatus` |  |  | Only runs in these statuses (list view), e.g. ['failed', 'completed_unverified']. |
| `cursor` | string |  |  | Page cursor: next_cursor from the previous call (same other arguments). |
| `limit` | integer |  |  | Page size for the list view (default 20, max 100). |
| `view` | `"list"` \| `"grid"` |  | `"list"` | 'list' (default): one row per run. 'grid': rows × cols code matrix of the main runs. |
| `rows` | array of string |  |  | Grid row axes (default: the treatment axes, e.g. ['method']). |
| `cols` | array of string |  |  | Grid column axes (default: ['seed']). At most 64 columns. |
| `metric` | string |  |  | Metric name to show in V grid cells, e.g. 'acc' (validated evaluations only). |
| `changed_since` | string |  |  | changes_cursor from an earlier call: return only runs with events after it. |

`RunStatus`: Summary status of a Run for listings, derived from its latest Attempt.

`"prepared"` \| `"submitting"` \| `"queued"` \| `"running"` \| `"succeeded"` \| `"completed_unverified"` \| `"failed"` \| `"cancelled"` \| `"rejected"` \| `"unknown"`

**Result `data` fields**

`view`: `"list"` | `"grid"`, `runs`?: array of `RunRow`, `grid`?: `GridData` | null, `total`: integer, `counts`: object of integer, `foreign_jobs`?: array of `ForeignJobs`, `changes_cursor`?: string | null.

(`?` = optional. Nested types are in the tool's `outputSchema`.)

### run_inspect

**Inspect a run** — read-only · idempotent · open-world · controller method `run_inspect` (`hpclab.services.runs:run_inspect`)

Everything known about one run: spec (argv, resources) and code/commit refs; every attempt with its Slurm job identity and the three separate state axes (scheduler_state, app_state, result_state); requeue segments; decoded pending reason; progress/ETA vs remaining walltime; GPU health flags (advisory); a deterministic diagnosis of failures with evidence lines; environment drift; artifacts and evaluations; and recommended_next (exact follow-up calls). Each attempt carries the `version` that run_cancel needs as expected_version. refresh=true asks for a bounded fresh observation; probe='gpu' samples nvidia-smi inside the running job (rate-limited). job_ref={cluster_id, job_id} finds the run behind a Slurm job id. Give exactly one of run_id, attempt_id, job_ref.

**Parameters**

| name | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `run_id` | string |  |  | Run to inspect (shows its latest attempt in focus). |
| `attempt_id` | string |  |  | Inspect the run of this attempt, focused on this attempt. |
| `job_ref` | `JobRef` |  |  | Reverse lookup by Slurm job, e.g. {"cluster_id": "hai", "job_id": "123456"}; add submit_time when job ids were reused. |
| `refresh` | boolean |  | `false` | Ask the controller for a fresh bounded observation first (returns cached data with stale=true if it times out). |
| `probe` | `"gpu"` |  |  | 'gpu' to sample GPU utilization/memory inside the running job's own allocation (rate-limited to 1 per 10 min per attempt). |

`JobRef`: External job identity for reverse lookup (job ids are not global identities).

| field | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cluster_id` | string | yes |  | Cluster the job ran on. |
| `job_id` | string | yes |  | Slurm job id. |
| `submit_time` | string |  |  | Submit time (ISO) to disambiguate reused job ids. |

**Result `data` fields**

`run`: `RunSummary`, `spec`: `SpecSummary`, `refs`: `Refs`, `focus_attempt_id`: string | null, `attempts`: array of `AttemptView`, `attempts_total`: integer, `operations`: array of `OperationSummary`, `pending`?: `PendingInfo` | null, `progress`?: `Progress` | null, `health`?: `Health` | null, `diagnosis`?: `Diagnosis` | null, `env`?: `EnvView` | null, `artifacts`?: `ArtifactsSummary` | null, `evaluations`?: array of `EvaluationRef`, `gpu_probe`?: `GpuProbeView` | null, `recommended_next`?: array of string, `stale`?: boolean.

(`?` = optional. Nested types are in the tool's `outputSchema`.)

### run_logs

**Read run logs** — read-only · idempotent · open-world · controller method `run_logs` (`hpclab.services.logs:run_logs`)

Read an attempt's stdout or stderr, bounded (default 32 KiB, max 64 KiB per call). tail_lines=N returns the last N lines (best for errors); otherwise read forward from cursor and continue with next_cursor. rotated=true means the file was replaced and reading restarted at 0. A missing file usually means the job has not started (a note, not an error). Does not wait for new output. For failures prefer run_inspect first: its diagnosis already quotes the decisive lines.

**Parameters**

| name | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `attempt_id` | string | yes |  | Attempt whose logs to read (attempts[].attempt_id from run_inspect, or latest_attempt.attempt_id from runs_list). |
| `stream` | `"stdout"` \| `"stderr"` |  | `"stdout"` | 'stdout' (default) or 'stderr'. Python tracebacks and Slurm errors are on stderr. |
| `cursor` | string |  |  | next_cursor from the previous call, to continue reading forward (not with tail_lines). |
| `max_bytes` | integer |  |  | Max bytes to return (default 32768, max 65536). |
| `tail_lines` | integer |  |  | Return only the last N lines (max 10000), e.g. 80. Do not combine with cursor. |

**Result `data` fields**

`attempt_id`: string, `stream`: `"stdout"` | `"stderr"`, `text`: string, `cursor`: string | null, `offset`: integer, `next_offset`: integer, `generation`: integer | null, `size`: integer | null, `truncated`: boolean, `rotated`: boolean, `eof`: boolean, `note`?: string | null.

(`?` = optional. Nested types are in the tool's `outputSchema`.)

### run_cancel

**Cancel an attempt** — mutating · destructive · idempotent · open-world · controller method `run_cancel` (`hpclab.services.submission:run_cancel`)

Cancel one attempt after re-verifying its live Slurm identity (job id, owner, submit token, submit time) right before scancel — any mismatch cancels nothing (cancel_state refused). Not yet submitted: cancelled immediately. Submission in flight/uncertain: the intent is recorded and applied after reconciliation. cancel_state goes 'requested' (intent recorded) -> 'sent' (identity-checked scancel issued) -> 'confirmed' (a later observation shows the job terminal; a job found already ended is confirmed with nothing sent). 'failed' means nothing was cancelled: the scheduler refused the scancel, the job never became visible in squeue/sacct, the adapter cannot cancel, or an abandon dropped the pending request. mode='request_checkpoint' sends the declared checkpoint signal instead (only for runs declaring resilience.stop_behavior=checkpoint_and_exit). Never use raw scancel. Destroys running work: confirm with the user.

**Parameters**

| name | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `attempt_id` | string | yes |  | Attempt to cancel (attempts[].attempt_id from run_inspect). |
| `expected_version` | integer | yes |  | The attempt's current version (attempts[].version from run_inspect). A stale version gets version_conflict with details.current_version. |
| `idempotency_key` | string | yes |  | Your key for this request. Retrying with the same key and arguments (e.g. after a lost reply) returns the original result; reusing it with other arguments is rejected. Use a new key for a new request. |
| `reason` | string |  |  | Why it is cancelled (recorded in the ledger). |
| `mode` | `"cancel"` \| `"request_checkpoint"` |  | `"cancel"` | 'cancel' (default) or 'request_checkpoint' (ask the job to checkpoint and exit). |

**Result `data` fields**

`attempt_id`: string, `run_id`: string, `phase`: string, `cancel_state`: string, `cancel_mode`?: string | null, `attempt_version`: integer, `operation_ref`?: string | null, `operation_id`?: string | null, `poll_after_ms`?: integer | null, `note`?: string.

(`?` = optional. Nested types are in the tool's `outputSchema`.)

### run_recover

**Plan a recovery** — mutating · idempotent · open-world · controller method `run_recover` (`hpclab.services.recovery:run_recover`)

Diagnose a stopped attempt and build a recovery execution plan for the SAME run — never submits. strategy: retry (same resources; excludes nodes implicated by 2+ attempts), resume (from a validated checkpoint; may first create a checkpoint probe run to submit), adjust_resources (e.g. more mem after host_oom, more time after timeout; resource_patch or the diagnosis hint). Default: the strategy the diagnosis suggests. Returns eligible, blocking reasons, diagnosis, the new resources and exec_plan_hash → submit with run_submit(run_id, execution_plan_hash) after the user agrees. Active or submission-uncertain attempts are never eligible. Scientific changes (smaller batch after CUDA OOM, lower lr after NaN) are not recoveries: derive a new run with experiment_prepare(derive_from=...). selector={workflow_id, cells: 'missing_valid'} plans every broken cell of a workflow at once → dispatch with workflow_submit(plan_id=<returned plan_id>).

**Parameters**

| name | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `idempotency_key` | string | yes |  | Your key for this request. Retrying with the same key and arguments (e.g. after a lost reply) returns the original result; reusing it with other arguments is rejected. Use a new key for a new request. |
| `attempt_id` | string |  |  | Stopped attempt to recover (the failed attempt_id from run_inspect or runs_list). Give this or selector. |
| `selector` | `RecoverySelector` |  |  | Batch recovery over a workflow, e.g. {"workflow_id": "wf_...", "cells": "missing_valid"}; cells may also be {"diagnosis_in": ["node_fail"]} or {"run_ids": ["run_..."]}. |
| `strategy` | `"retry"` \| `"resume"` \| `"adjust_resources"` |  |  | 'retry', 'resume' or 'adjust_resources' (default: suggested by the diagnosis). |
| `checkpoint_ref` | string |  |  | Checkpoint artifact (id or hpclab://artifacts/<id>, role checkpoint) to resume from (default: the newest valid one of this run). |
| `resource_patch` | `ResourcePatch` |  |  | Resource changes for adjust_resources (or resume), e.g. {"mem": "16G"} or {"time": "12:00:00"}. Validated against partition limits. |

`RecoverySelector`: Batch recovery over the cells of one workflow.

| field | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `workflow_id` | string | yes |  | Workflow whose cells to recover. |
| `cells` | `"missing_valid"` \| `DiagnosisSelector` \| `RunIdsSelector` |  | `"missing_valid"` | 'missing_valid' (default: every cell without a valid result), {diagnosis_in: [codes]} or {run_ids: [ids]}. |

`DiagnosisSelector`

| field | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `diagnosis_in` | array of string | yes |  | Diagnosis codes to select, e.g. ['node_fail', 'timeout']. |

`RunIdsSelector`

| field | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `run_ids` | array of string | yes |  | Run ids to select. |

`ResourcePatch`: Resource fields a recovery may change. Everything else about the Run stays frozen.

| field | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `time` | string |  |  | New time limit, e.g. '12:00:00'. |
| `mem` | string |  |  | New memory per node, e.g. '64G'. |
| `gpus` | integer (0..64) |  |  | New GPU count. |
| `gpu_type` | string |  |  | New GPU type. |
| `partition` | string |  |  | New partition. |
| `account` | string |  |  | New Slurm account. |
| `qos` | string |  |  | New QoS. |
| `cpus` | integer (1..512) |  |  | New CPUs per task. |
| `nodes` | integer (1..64) |  |  | New node count. |
| `ntasks_per_node` | integer (1..64) |  |  | New tasks per node. |
| `exclude_nodes` | array of string |  |  | Nodes to avoid, e.g. ['node-12']. |
| `constraint` | string |  |  | Slurm --constraint expression. |
| `extra_sbatch` | array of string |  |  | Extra raw #SBATCH options. |

### artifact_read

**Read an artifact** — read-only · idempotent · open-world · controller method `artifact_read` (`hpclab.services.artifacts:artifact_read`)

Bounded, integrity-checked read of one artifact. Default view by type: .jsonl and metrics logs → jsonl_tail (last records, parsed), .json → json (parsed), others → head. A directory artifact returns its member files instead (read a member by its artifact_id). Refuses paths escaping the attempt directory; returns 'stale' if the file changed since it was indexed (never silently reads new content); binary files return metadata plus a download operation. Numbers for papers come from evaluations/evidence bundles, not from reading artifacts.

| `view` | `"head"` \| `"tail"` \| `"text"` \| `"json"` \| `"jsonl_tail"` |  |  | head \| tail \| text \| json \| jsonl_tail (default chosen from the file type). |
| `max_bytes` | integer |  |  | Max bytes to read (default 32768, max 65536). |

| field | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `offset` | integer (0..) |  | `0` | Start byte (default 0). |
| `length` | integer (1..) |  |  | Number of bytes (capped by max_bytes). |

### evaluation_collect

**Collect metrics** — mutating · idempotent · open-world · controller method `evaluation_collect` (`hpclab.services.evaluations:evaluation_collect`)

### results_compare

**Compare results** — mutating · idempotent · closed-world · controller method `results_compare` (`hpclab.services.compare:results_compare`)

Compare methods over the PLANNED run set: every planned main run appears as included, missing, failed or excluded (exclusions need reasons and are disclosed) — the denominator is the plan, not what happened to finish. Per group and metric: n/expected_n, mean, sample std, SEM, t-CI, min/max and per-seed values; descriptive differences vs the baseline (paired by seed); comparability problems (different split/evaluator/dataset); selection leaks; and an integrity section (post-hoc seeds, mixed GPU types or code versions). No significance claims. Archived as an immutable comparison (comparison_id). Next: evidence_export(comparison_ref=<comparison_id>).

**Parameters**

| name | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `planned_run_set_ref` | string | yes |  | experiment_id, plan_id or workflow_id defining the planned denominator (usually the experiment_id). |
| `metric_names` | array of string | yes |  | Metrics to compare, e.g. ['acc', 'loss'] (names from the evaluations / spec.comparison.metrics). |
| `expected_seeds` | array of integer |  |  | Seeds the plan must contain, e.g. [1, 2, 3]; a mismatch with the plan is an error (guards against a wrong run set). |
| `comparison_contract` | `ComparisonContract` |  |  | Override the spec's comparison contract: {treatment, invariants, baseline, metrics, pair_by_seed, ci_level, selection, attempt_selection, min_n, bold_rule}. |
| `evaluation_refs` | array of string |  |  | Use exactly these evaluation ids (e.g. from a custom evaluator) instead of the default selection. |
| `exclusions` | array of `ExclusionSpec` |  |  | [{run_id, reason}] planned runs to exclude from the statistics; each is disclosed with its reason. |
| `idempotency_key` | string |  |  | Optional. Your key for this request. Retrying with the same key and arguments (e.g. after a lost reply) returns the original result; reusing it with other arguments is rejected. Use a new key for a new request. |

`ComparisonContract`: What may differ (treatment) and what must match (invariants) between compared runs.

| field | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `treatment` | array of string |  |  | Axes that may differ between groups, e.g. ['method']. |
| `invariants` | array of string |  |  | Properties that must match across compared results (default split, evaluator, dataset). |
| `baseline` | object of string \| integer \| number \| boolean \| null |  |  | Treatment values of the baseline group, e.g. {"method": "baseline"}. |
| `metrics` | array of `MetricDecl` |  |  | Metric declarations: [{name, higher_is_better, unit}]. |
| `pair_by_seed` | boolean |  | `true` | Pair differences by seed (default true). |
| `ci_level` | number |  | `0.95` | Confidence level of intervals (default 0.95). |
| `selection` | `SelectionRule` |  |  | Which record a reported number comes from. |
| `attempt_selection` | `"latest_valid"` \| `"first_valid"` |  | `"latest_valid"` | Which valid attempt of a run counts: latest_valid (default) or first_valid. |
| `min_n` | integer (1..) |  | `1` | Minimum included seeds per cell before a value is reported (default 1). |
| `bold_rule` | `"none"` \| `"best_mean"` |  | `"none"` | 'none' (default) or 'best_mean'. |

`MetricDecl`

| field | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes |  | Metric name, e.g. 'acc'. |
| `higher_is_better` | boolean |  |  | Direction of improvement. |
| `unit` | string |  |  | Unit, e.g. 'fraction' or 'nats'. |

`SelectionRule`: Which record/checkpoint a reported number comes from. Selecting the best checkpoint on the same split that is reported is a leakage risk; ``results_compare`` refuses it (``selection_leak``) unless explicitly declared otherwise.

| field | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rule` | `"final"` \| `"last"` \| `"best_by"` \| `"at_step"` |  | `"final"` | 'final' (the record marked final, default), 'last', 'best_by' (needs select_metric/select_split/mode) or 'at_step'. |
| `select_metric` | string |  |  | Metric used to pick the record for best_by. |

| `step` | integer |  |  | Step for at_step. |
| `report_split` | string |  |  | Split whose values are reported. |

| field | type | required | default | description |

| `run_id` | string | yes |  | Planned run to exclude. |
| `reason` | string | yes |  | Concrete reason (disclosed in the bundle). |

### evidence_export

**Export an evidence bundle** — mutating · idempotent · closed-world · controller method `evidence_export` (`hpclab.services.evidence:evidence_export`)

Build a paper-ready evidence bundle from a comparison: Markdown summary, LaTeX booktabs table (cells are \hpcval{<bundle>:<cell>}{value} so numbers stay verifiable; the preamble makes the macro print just the value; cells with missing seeds are footnoted), long-format CSV and a JSON manifest tracing every value to evaluation → artifact digest → attempt → Slurm job → run spec → code commit → environment. Files are resources: hpclab://evidence/<bundle_id>/table.tex, summary.md, table.csv, manifest.json. Incomplete coverage still exports, with warnings. Give comparison_ref, or planned_run_set_ref (+ optional metric_names) to compare and export in one call. Next: paste table.tex into the paper, later evidence_verify(bundle_ref, tex_paths) to catch stale numbers.

| `evaluation_refs` | array of string |  |  | With planned_run_set_ref: use exactly these evaluation ids. |
| `formats` | array of `"md"` \| `"json"` \| `"csv"` \| `"latex"` |  |  | Subset of md, json, csv, latex (default: all). |
| `table_spec` | `TableSpec` |  |  | LaTeX table layout, e.g. {"cols": ["acc"], "decimals": 1, "scale": 100, "stat": "mean_std"}. |
| `metric_names` | array of string |  |  | With planned_run_set_ref: metrics to compare, e.g. ['acc'] (default: the spec's comparison.metrics). |

`TableSpec`: How the LaTeX table displays the comparison (the bundle itself always has everything).

| field | type | required | default | description |

### evidence_verify

**Verify evidence and paper numbers** — read-only · idempotent · closed-world · controller method `evidence_verify` (`hpclab.services.verify:evidence_verify`)

Check an evidence bundle and a manuscript before submission: recomputes the bundle's aggregates from the per-seed evaluations and checks every \hpcval-tagged number in the .tex against the bundle and the current ledger. Findings (severity error|warn|info): STALE_TEX_NUMBER (newer results differ → re-compare and re-export), VALUE_MISMATCH (hand-edited number), AGGREGATE_MISMATCH, N_BELOW_EXPECTED_UNFOOTNOTED, SEED_SELECTION, MIXED_CODE_DIGEST, MIXED_GPU_TYPE, INVARIANT_MISMATCH, SELECTION_LEAK, ARTIFACT_DIGEST_CHANGED, UNRESOLVED_REF, NO_TAGS_FOUND (no tag: NOT checked), UNRESOLVED_INPUT (an \input that could not be read), UNTAGGED_TEX_NUMBER. Read-only. Verifies record consistency, not scientific correctness. In a new session the bundle id can be read from the .tex itself: \hpcval{<bundle_id>:<cell>}{...}.

**Parameters**

| name | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bundle_ref` | string | yes |  | bundle_id from evidence_export, or hpclab://evidence/<id>. |
| `tex_paths` | array of string |  |  | LaTeX files to check, e.g. ['paper/main.tex'] (relative paths resolve against the agent's working directory). Files they \input/\include/\subfile/\import are scanned too (files_scanned in the result). |
| `tex_content` | string |  |  | LaTeX source as a string (alternative to tex_paths). |
| `recheck_remote` | boolean |  | `false` | Also re-hash small output files on the cluster (bounded; network I/O). Default false. |

### workflow_cancel

**Cancel a workflow** — mutating · destructive · idempotent · open-world · controller method `workflow_cancel` (`hpclab.services.workflows:workflow_cancel`)

Stop a matrix: closes dispatch atomically and cancels never-dispatched cells. scope='queued_only' (default) leaves submitted jobs running; scope='all_managed' also cancels every active cell, each after a live identity check. Submissions in flight or uncertain are reconciled first, never assumed cancelled. expected_version must be the workflow's current version (it changes as dispatch proceeds; read hpclab://workflows/<workflow_id> right before). Returns per-cell cancel states. Confirm with the user.

**Parameters**

| name | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `workflow_id` | string | yes |  | Workflow to cancel (workflow_id from workflow_submit). |
| `expected_version` | integer | yes |  | The workflow's current version (from hpclab://workflows/<workflow_id>). A stale version gets version_conflict with details.current_version. |
| `scope` | `"queued_only"` \| `"all_managed"` |  | `"queued_only"` | 'queued_only' (default): stop dispatching, cancel undispatched cells. 'all_managed': also cancel running/queued jobs. |
| `idempotency_key` | string | yes |  | Your key for this request. Retrying with the same key and arguments (e.g. after a lost reply) returns the original result; reusing it with other arguments is rejected. Use a new key for a new request. |

**Result `data` fields**

`workflow_id`: string, `workflow_ref`: string, `operation_id`: string | null, `operation_ref`: string | null, `poll_after_ms`?: integer, `scope`: string, `state`: string, `dispatch_state`: string, `version`: integer, `counts`: object of integer, `cells`?: array of `CancelCellView`, `budget_kept_gpu_hours`?: number | null, `notes`?: array of string.

(`?` = optional. Nested types are in the tool's `outputSchema`.)

### usage_report

**GPU usage report** — read-only · idempotent · open-world · controller method `usage_report` (`hpclab.services.usage:usage_report`)

Allocated GPU-hours (GPUs × wall time, not utilization) from Slurm accounting for me (scope='self') or a lab account (scope='account') over a window (default: last 7 days, max 93), grouped by user/partition/gpu_type/state/..., with waste by cause (diagnosis class for hpclab runs), median queue wait and walltime accuracy. `visibility` says whether other users' jobs were visible: when it is 'self_only' (PrivateData hides them) there are no lab totals — say so instead of presenting a partial sum. Long windows may return partial results (coverage incomplete; call again to continue). Not a leaderboard.

**Parameters**

| name | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cluster_id` | string | yes |  | Registered cluster id. |
| `scope` | `"self"` \| `"account"` |  | `"self"` | 'self' (default): my jobs. 'account': all visible jobs of a Slurm account. |
| `account` | string |  |  | Slurm account for scope='account' (default: the overlay's account). |
| `since` | string |  |  | Window start: ISO date/time or relative like '7d', '24h', '30m' (default 7d ago). |
| `until` | string |  |  | Window end: ISO date/time or relative (default now). |
| `group_by` | array of `"user"` \| `"account"` \| `"partition"` \| `"qos"` \| `"gpu_type"` \| `"state"` \| `"diagnosis_class"` |  |  | Grouping dimensions (default ['partition'] for self, ['user'] for account). |
| `include` | array of `"now"` \| `"waste"` \| `"queue_wait"` \| `"walltime_accuracy"` |  |  | Extra sections: now (current queue), waste, queue_wait, walltime_accuracy (default: all but now). |
| `limit` | integer |  |  | Max rows (default 20, max 100). |

**Result `data` fields**

`cluster_id`: string, `scope`: `"self"` | `"account"`, `account`: string | null, `user`: string, `since`: string, `until`: string, `group_by`: array of string, `include`: array of string, `visibility`: `"full"` | `"self_only"` | `"unavailable"`, `private_data`: string | null, `rows`: array of `UsageRow`, `rows_total`: integer, `rows_truncated`: integer, `totals`: object of `UsageStats`, `now`?: `NowSection` | null, `details`: `UsageDetails`, `notes`?: array of string.

(`?` = optional. Nested types are in the tool's `outputSchema`.)

## Resources

Read with `resources/read`. They share the tools' size limits; text resources that were cut
end with a visible truncation marker. `resources/list` returns `hpclab://experiments` plus the
20 most recent experiments, so a new session can find experiment ids.

| URI | MIME type | controller method | content |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hpclab://operations/{operation_id}` | `application/json` | `operation_get` | Background operation: kind, state, stage, error, progress (never faked), result refs, suggested poll interval. |
| `hpclab://experiments` | `application/json` | `experiments_list` | Experiments in the ledger, newest first (experiment_id, name, cluster, status, run and plan counts). |
| `hpclab://experiments/{experiment_id}` | `application/json` | `experiment_get` | Experiment spec, plans, run counts by cell code, budget summary. |
| `hpclab://plans/{plan_id}/script/full` | `text/x-shellscript` | `plan_script` | The complete sbatch script (incl. the static hpclab wrapper runtime) of the plan's first main run. |
| `hpclab://plans/{plan_id}/script` | `text/x-shellscript` | `plan_script` | The run-specific part of the sbatch script of the plan's first main run (#SBATCH directives, argv, env, setup) for review; the static wrapper is replaced by a marker (see /script/full). |
| `hpclab://plans/{plan_id}` | `application/json` | `plan_get` | Frozen runs with their RunSpec and execution plan, hashes, validation findings, budget (first 20 runs). |
| `hpclab://workflows/{workflow_id}/grid` | `application/json` | `runs_list` | Treatment × seed grid of a workflow with cell codes. |
| `hpclab://workflows/{workflow_id}` | `application/json` | `workflow_get` | Workflow state, dispatch state and current version (for workflow_cancel / resume), gate, breaker evidence, per-cell states, budget. |
| `hpclab://runs/{run_id}` | `application/json` | `run_inspect` | Same as run_inspect(run_id) without refresh. |
| `hpclab://artifacts/{artifact_id}` | `application/json` | `artifact_get` | Artifact metadata: path, size, digest, integrity and producing attempt. |
| `hpclab://evaluations/{evaluation_id}` | `application/json` | `evaluation_get` | Evaluation: metrics, evaluator and config, input digests, validation, provenance. |
| `hpclab://comparisons/{comparison_id}` | `application/json` | `comparison_get` | Archived comparison: planned run set, coverage, statistics, differences, contract, integrity. |
| `hpclab://evidence/{bundle_id}/{file}` | `text/plain` | `evidence_get` | One evidence file: summary.md, table.tex, table.csv or manifest.json. |
| `hpclab://evidence/{bundle_id}` | `application/json` | `evidence_get` | Evidence bundle metadata, coverage and file list. |
| `hpclab://trace/{cell_ref}` | `application/json` | `trace` | Full provenance chain of one table cell (<bundle_id>:<cell_id>, as in the \hpcval tags): per-seed value → evaluation → artifact digest → attempt → Slurm job → run spec → code → environment. |

## Prompts

For MCP clients without skill support: each prompt returns the matching skill from `skills/`
(the same text `hpclab skills install` copies into `~/.claude/skills`).

| prompt | skill | arguments (`?` optional) | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `plan_experiment` | `hpclab-experiment-design` | `goal` | Design and launch an experiment (baseline, treatments × seeds, metrics, smoke gate, budget). |
| `diagnose_run` | `hpclab-run-doctor` | `run_id` | Triage a failed, pending, stuck or uncertain run and plan the smallest correct recovery. |
| `write_results` | `hpclab-paper-evidence` | `experiment_id`, `tex_path`? | Collect, compare and export a traceable results table and paragraph; verify a manuscript's numbers. |
| `onboard_cluster` | `hpclab-cluster-onboarding` | `cluster_id`? | Set up and verify a cluster for HPC Lab. |
| `lab_overview` | `hpclab-lab-overview` | `account`?, `cluster_id`? | Honest GPU usage and experiment progress overview for a lab. |
